hints: Look closely at the name peroxyacetyl nitrate, what elements must be in it and where could they come from?
The nitrate part needs a nitrogen source from the list, while the acetyl part needs a carbon and hydrogen source.
Remember which two primary pollutants mix in sunlight to make photochemical smog products like ozone and PAN.
walkthrough:
**Recall what PAN is**

Think of PAN as a secondary pollutant of photochemical smog. It is not emitted directly, it is made in the air in strong sunlight.

$$\text{primary pollutants} \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} \text{PAN} + \text{O}_3$$

**Match the name to the reactants**

The name tells you the recipe. Nitrate means it must contain nitrogen and oxygen, so you need nitrogen oxides, $\text{NO}_x$. Acetyl ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$) means it must contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, so you need hydrocarbons.

$$\text{NO}_2 + \text{unburnt hydrocarbons} \xrightarrow{\text{uv light}} \text{CH}_3\text{COOONO}_2 \text{ (PAN)}$$

**Check the pair**

That is pollutant 1 (nitrogen oxides) plus pollutant 3 (unburnt hydrocarbons). Carbon monoxide and sulfur dioxide are involved in other pollution problems, not in making PAN.

options.A: Correct. Nitrogen oxides (1) provide the N and O for the nitrate part, and unburnt hydrocarbons (3) provide the C, H and O for the peroxyacetyl part. Together in sunlight they form PAN as part of photochemical smog.
options.B: Incorrect. Sulfur dioxide (4) causes acid rain by forming sulfuric acid, it does not supply carbon and hydrogen to make the acetyl group in PAN. This choice mixes up two different pollution stories.
options.C: Incorrect. Carbon monoxide (2) and hydrocarbons (3) contain no nitrogen, so they cannot make a nitrate. Students choosing this forget to check that PAN must contain nitrogen.
options.D: Incorrect. Carbon monoxide (2) leads to photochemical smog and toxic effects, and sulfur dioxide (4) leads to acid rain, but neither combination provides both nitrogen and hydrocarbons needed for PAN.
